evals.prompt: I have a branch that adds a new /reports API endpoint. While I was in there I also upgraded the web framework to its next major version and reformatted about 30 files that the linter flagged. Help me get this ready to open as a pull request.
assertions: Advises splitting the work into separate PRs rather than opening it as one (e.g. reformat, framework upgrade, and new endpoint as distinct PRs)
Recommends a target size around 50-200 changed lines (treating roughly 400 as a soft cap), or frames the goal as keeping review time under about an hour

evals.prompt: Write the 'how I tested this' section for my PR. The change fixes a bug where an import step double-charged on retry. All I really did to check it was run it locally and it worked.
assertions: Rejects or replaces the bare 'tested locally' phrasing with concrete evidence: names the specific environment, the exact scenario, and the observed result
For the fix, states how the bug was confirmed before the change and how the fix was confirmed after
Includes an explicit way to reproduce end to end (a command, request, or link) and/or edge cases checked

evals.prompt: Draft a reusable pull request description template for our repo so people stop opening PRs with an empty body.
assertions: Produces a lean template of roughly 4-6 prompts/sections rather than a long mandatory checkbox form
Includes distinct sections covering what changed, why (work item/issue link), how tested, and tradeoffs/risks
Includes a section for linking related/sibling PRs or the shared work item

evals.prompt: My PR is a single large diff: a database schema migration plus all the application code that depends on the new columns. It's about 500 lines and can't really be broken apart. What should I do before requesting review?
assertions: Confirms an atomic, unsplittable change (migration plus dependent code) is acceptable even when large, rather than forcing a split
Says to explicitly flag in the PR that it is one atomic unit and explain why it cannot be split
Advises self-review of the full diff and keeping it a draft until CI is green before flipping to ready and assigning reviewers
